results.question: How many completed orders did each distribution center handle in 2024?
results.golden_sql: SELECT d.name AS distribution_center, COUNT(*) AS realized_orders FROM `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_orders` o JOIN `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_distribution_centers` d ON o.distribution_center_id = d.id WHERE o.is_realized_order = TRUE AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.created_at) = 2024 GROUP BY d.name ORDER BY realized_orders DESC;
results.generated_sql:
SELECT
    dc.name AS distribution_center,
    COUNT(o.order_id) AS completed_orders
FROM silver_layer.stg_orders AS o
JOIN silver_layer.stg_distribution_centers AS dc
    ON o.distribution_center_id = dc.id
WHERE LOWER(o.status) IN ('complete', 'completed')
  AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.created_at) = 2024
GROUP BY dc.name
ORDER BY completed_orders DESC;
results.judge_reason: The generated query filters on status IN ('complete','completed') instead of the is_realized_order = TRUE business-rule flag. That flag likely covers a different set of statuses (for example, Shipped orders that are not Cancelled or Returned), so the counts would probably differ.

results.question: Which product category made the most profit in 2024?
results.golden_sql: SELECT p.category, ROUND(SUM(oi.gross_margin_amount), 2) AS gross_margin FROM `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_order_items` oi JOIN `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_products` p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE oi.is_realized_revenue = TRUE AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM oi.created_at) = 2024 GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY gross_margin DESC LIMIT 1;
results.generated_sql:
SELECT
    p.category,
    SUM(oi.gross_margin_amount) AS total_profit
FROM silver_layer.stg_order_items AS oi
JOIN silver_layer.stg_products AS p
    ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE oi.is_realized_revenue = TRUE
  AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM oi.created_at) = 2024
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY total_profit DESC
LIMIT 1;
results.judge_reason: The generated query uses the same tables, join, is_realized_revenue filter, 2024 year filter, gross_margin_amount aggregation, grouping and top-1 ordering as the ground truth; only rounding and the project prefix differ.

results.question: Which distribution centers have the most orders with impossible shipping dates?
results.golden_sql: SELECT d.name AS distribution_center, COUNTIF(a.has_timeline_anomaly) AS anomaly_orders FROM `apex-activewear.silver_layer.int_order_attribution` a JOIN `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_orders` o ON a.order_id = o.order_id JOIN `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_distribution_centers` d ON o.distribution_center_id = d.id GROUP BY d.name ORDER BY anomaly_orders DESC;
results.generated_sql:
SELECT
    dc.id AS distribution_center_id,
    dc.name AS distribution_center_name,
    COUNT(o.order_id) AS impossible_shipping_orders
FROM silver_layer.stg_orders AS o
JOIN silver_layer.stg_distribution_centers AS dc
    ON o.distribution_center_id = dc.id
WHERE o.shipped_at < o.created_at
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY impossible_shipping_orders DESC
results.judge_reason: The generated query hand-rolls a single check (shipped_at < created_at) instead of using the has_timeline_anomaly flag from int_order_attribution, which likely covers more impossible-timeline conditions, so the counts per distribution center can differ.

results.question: How much did each paying customer spend on average in 2023, by acquisition source?
results.golden_sql: SELECT u.acquisition_source, ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(oi.sale_price), COUNT(DISTINCT oi.user_id)), 2) AS revenue_per_customer FROM `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_order_items` oi JOIN `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_users` u ON oi.user_id = u.user_id WHERE oi.is_realized_revenue = TRUE AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM oi.created_at) = 2023 GROUP BY u.acquisition_source ORDER BY revenue_per_customer DESC;
results.generated_sql:
SELECT
    u.acquisition_source,
    SUM(oi.sale_price) / COUNT(DISTINCT oi.user_id) AS avg_spend_per_customer
FROM silver_layer.stg_order_items AS oi
JOIN silver_layer.stg_users AS u
    ON oi.user_id = u.user_id
WHERE oi.is_realized_revenue = TRUE
  AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM oi.created_at) = 2023
GROUP BY u.acquisition_source
ORDER BY avg_spend_per_customer DESC;
results.judge_reason: The generated query uses the same tables, join, is_realized_revenue filter, 2023 filter, grouping and metric (revenue / distinct paying customers) as the ground truth; it differs only in rounding, SAFE_DIVIDE and the lack of project qualification.

results.question: How many website events did each traffic source generate in 2024, counting only activity after the user signed up?
results.golden_sql: SELECT oe.traffic_source, COUNT(*) AS events FROM `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_online_events` oe JOIN `apex-activewear.silver_layer.stg_users` u ON oe.user_id = u.user_id WHERE oe.created_at >= u.created_at AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM oe.created_at) = 2024 GROUP BY oe.traffic_source ORDER BY events DESC;
results.generated_sql:
SELECT
    e.traffic_source,
    COUNT(*) AS total_events
FROM silver_layer.stg_online_events AS e
INNER JOIN silver_layer.stg_users AS u
    ON e.user_id = u.user_id
WHERE e.created_at >= u.created_at
  AND e.created_at >= '2024-01-01'
  AND e.created_at < '2025-01-01'
GROUP BY e.traffic_source
ORDER BY total_events DESC;
results.judge_reason: The generated query uses the same tables, the same inner join on user_id, the same post-signup filter (event created_at >= user created_at) and the same grouping by traffic_source. Its 2024 date range is equivalent to EXTRACT(YEAR ...) = 2024.
